advances: An exact rational mass-growing single-double endpoint family with all three actual lower crossings and both endpoint tails is rejected by the joint geometry of \(U_1,U_2,V\).  For every integer \(D\ge18\), the exact hull \(H=\operatorname{conv}(U_1\cup U_2\cup V)\) has \(|H|>M+m\), so compatibility already contradicts the residual no-half inequality \(k<M+m\).  More sharply, the complete weighted \(R^\star\)-charge carried by \(H\) is strictly larger than \(2p_\varnothing\).  This is a calibrated family lemma, not a universal three-body hull inequality.
author: mp_r365_single_double_triplehull
proof:
Put
\[
 p_i=f_i-L_i.
\]
At the three displayed vertices of \(A_0\), the triples
\((p_1,p_2,p_3)\) are respectively
\[
 \left(-1,\frac{D+1}{2},\frac{D+1}{2}\right),\quad
 \left(\frac{D+1}{2},-1,\frac{D+1}{2}\right),\quad
 \left(\frac{D+1}{2},\frac{D+1}{2},-1\right).
\]
The area of \(A_0\) is \((D+3)^2/4\).  Each lower cap \(p_i\le0\)
is a corner triangle obtained by the linear ratio
\(2/(D+3)\) on both incident edges, and hence has area
\[
 \frac{(D+3)^2}{4}\left(\frac{2}{D+3}\right)^2=1.
\]
For \(D>1\), two such corner caps are disjoint up to their null
boundaries.  This proves all asserted \(P\)-cell areas.

For \(A_2\), put \(q_i=f_i+L_i\).  At its three displayed vertices,
\(q_3\) takes the values \(2,2,-2\); the line \(q_3=0\) cuts off the
top triangle \(Q_{123}\).  Direct intersection with the three lines
\(q_i=0\), followed by the triangle-area formula, gives
\[
 |Q_1|=|Q_2|=D,\qquad
 |Q_{123}|=2C,\qquad
 |A_2|=8C.
\]
The remaining positive chamber is \(Q_{12}\), of area
\[
 8C-2D-2C=4D+12.
\]
The three vertex signs are respectively \(1,2,123\), and the region
between them has type \(12\); convexity and the three cutting lines
show that no other \(Q\)-cell has positive area.  This proves the
support and area claims.

We next audit the full lower-crossing distributions, rather than only
their derivatives at the proposed levels.  By symmetry it suffices to
treat rows \(1\) and \(3\).

For row \(1\), the \(f_1\)-values on the vertices of \(A_0\) are
\(-1,(D+1)/2,(D+1)/2\).  Hence
\[
 |A_0\cap\{f_1\le a\}|=(a+1)^2
 \qquad(-1\le a\le0).
\]
On \(A_2\), the unique maximum of \(f_1\) is \(D/2\), and the other
two vertex values are \(-D/2\) and \(-(3D+8)/2\).  For
\(-D/2\le b\le D/2\), the upper corner above \(f_1=b\) has area
\[
 \frac{(D-2b)^2}{D}.
\]
Taking \(b=-a\), one obtains, for \(-1\le a\le0\),
\[
 \Phi_1(a)-\Phi_1(0)
 =
 \left(1-\frac4D\right)a^2-2a\ge0.
\]
For \(-D/2\le a\le-1\), the \(A_0\)-cap is empty and the
\(A_2\)-cap only increases as \(a\) decreases.  At \(a=-1\), its
excess over \(\Phi_1(0)\) is
\[
 3-\frac4D>0.
\]
For \(a\le-D/2\), the \(A_2\)-cap is all of \(A_2\), and
\[
 m-\Phi_1(0)=D-1>0.
\]
Thus \(\Phi_1(a)\ge\Phi_1(0)\) for every \(a\le0\).  On the other
hand, the same quadratic formula gives
\[
 \Phi_1(a)-\Phi_1(0)<0
 \quad\text{for}\quad
 0<a<\frac{2D}{D-4}.
\]
Therefore \(0=\inf\{a:\Phi_1(a)<\Phi_1(0)\}\).  Reflection in
\(s=0\) proves the identical assertion in row \(2\).

For row \(3\), write \(a=L_3+\varepsilon\).  The \(p_3\)-values on
\(A_0\) are again \(-1,(D+1)/2,(D+1)/2\), while the \(q_3\)-values
on \(A_2\) are \(-2,2,2\).  Thus, for
\(-1\le\varepsilon\le1\),
\[
 \Phi_3(L_3+\varepsilon)-\Phi_3(L_3)
 =
 -2(C-1)\varepsilon+\frac{C+2}{2}\varepsilon^2.
\]
This is nonnegative for \(-1\le\varepsilon\le0\), and it is negative
for
\[
 0<\varepsilon<\frac{4(C-1)}{C+2}.
\]
For \(\varepsilon\le-1\), the \(A_0\)-cap is empty and the
\(A_2\)-cap increases as \(\varepsilon\) decreases; its value at
\(\varepsilon=-1\) already exceeds the value at \(0\) by
\((5C-2)/2\).  Hence
\[
 L_3=\inf\{a:\Phi_3(a)<\Phi_3(L_3)\}.
\]
The displayed cell areas give
\[
 \Phi_1(0)=\Phi_2(0)=1+(m-D)=7D+17,
\qquad
 \Phi_3(L_3)=1+2C=2D+5,
\]
which proves all three strict tails.  This is exactly the lower-end
behavior isolated abstractly in accepted fact `624b129b68e0fdee`.

It remains to compute the joint midpoint hull.  The closed source
cells have the following vertices:
\[
 \overline{P_\varnothing}
 =
 \operatorname{conv}\left\{
 \left(\pm\frac{D-1}{2},\frac{D-1}{2}\right),
 \left(\pm\frac{D+1}{2},\frac{D+1}{2}\right),
 (\pm1,D)\right\},
\]
\[
 \overline{P_3}=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1,D),(0,D+1),(1,D)\},
\]
\[
 \overline{Q_1}
 =\operatorname{conv}\{(-2C,-C-2),(-C-2,-C-2),(-C,-C)\},
\]
\[
\overline{Q_2}=\rho(\overline{Q_1}),\qquad
\overline{Q_{123}}
=\operatorname{conv}\{(-C,-C),(0,-C+2),(C,-C)\},
\]
where \(\rho(s,t)=(-s,t)\).  Adding these polygons and dividing by
two gives
\[
 U_1=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
 \left(-\frac{5D+9}{4},-\frac{D+7}{4}\right),
 \left(-\frac{5D+7}{4},-\frac{D+9}{4}\right),
 \left(-\frac{2D+5}{2},-2\right),
 \right.
\]
\[
 \left.
 \left(-\frac{D+3}{2},-1\right),
 \left(-\frac{D+1}{2},-1\right),
 \left(-\frac{D+9}{4},-\frac{D+9}{4}\right),
 \left(-\frac{D+3}{4},-\frac{D+3}{4}\right)
 \right\},
\]
\[
U_2=\rho(U_1),
\]
and
\[
 V=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
 \left(-\frac{D+3}{2},-1\right),
 \left(-\frac C2,-\frac12\right),
 \left(0,\frac12\right),
 \left(\frac C2,-\frac12\right),
 \left(\frac{D+3}{2},-1\right)
 \right\}.
\]
On the right boundary from bottom to top, the successive slopes
\(ds/dt\) of the claimed nonagon are
\[
1,\quad -1,\quad-\frac{D+3}{3},\quad-\frac{D+2}{2},
\]
which are strictly decreasing.  Substitution of the \(t\)-coordinates
of every omitted vertex in the displayed lists for \(U_1,U_2,V\)
gives \(|s|\le w(t)\), where \(w\) is the affine interpolation of
these boundary vertices written below.  Thus, for \(D\ge18\), pruning
the nonextreme points gives exactly the nonagon listed in the
statement.

For an independent area and cell audit, its horizontal section at
height \(t\) is \([-w(t),w(t)]\).  Put
\[
 t_0=-\frac{D+9}{4},\qquad
 t_1=-\frac{D+7}{4}.
\]
The nonzero section range is \(t_0\le t\le1/2\), and the vertex list
gives
\[
 w(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 t+\dfrac{3D+8}{2},&t_0\le t\le t_1,\\[1mm]
 -t+\dfrac{2D+1}{2},&t_1\le t\le-2,\\[1mm]
 \dfrac{2D+3-2(D+3)t}{6},&-2\le t\le-\dfrac12,\\[2mm]
 \dfrac{(D+2)(1-2t)}4,&-\dfrac12\le t\le\dfrac12.
 \end{cases}
\]
Integrating \(2w(t)\) gives
\[
 |H|=\frac{9D^2+74D+113}{16}.
\]

The sign-cell cuts in these coordinates are especially simple.  For
\(t<-1\), the central interval \(t\le s\le-t\) is \(R_{12}\), with
the two side intervals in \(R_1,R_2\).  For \(-1\le t<0\), the same
central interval is \(R_{123}\), with side intervals in
\(R_{13},R_{23}\).  For \(t\ge0\), the central interval
\(-t<s<t\) is \(R_3\), with side intervals in \(R_{13},R_{23}\).
One checks from the displayed \(w\) that \(w(t)>-t\) on
\([t_0,0]\).  On \([0,1/2]\), the unique solution of \(w(t)=t\) is
\[
 \tau=\frac{D+2}{2(D+4)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 h_1=h_2=\int_{t_0}^{-1}(w(t)+t)\,dt,
\qquad
 h_{12}=\int_{t_0}^{-1}(-2t)\,dt,
\]
\[
 h_{123}=\int_{-1}^{0}(-2t)\,dt,
\]
\[
 h_{13}=h_{23}
 =\int_{-1}^{0}(w(t)+t)\,dt
 +\int_0^\tau(w(t)-t)\,dt,
\]
\[
 h_3=\int_0^\tau2t\,dt+\int_\tau^{1/2}2w(t)\,dt.
\]
Substitution of the four affine branches of \(w\) gives exactly
\[
 h_1=h_2=\frac{6D^2+29D+9}{24},\quad
 h_{12}=\frac{D^2+18D+65}{16},\quad
 h_{123}=1,
\]
\[
 h_{13}=h_{23}=
 \frac{13D^2+64D+54}{24(D+4)},\quad
 h_3=\frac{D+2}{4(D+4)}.
\]
This also independently verifies that their sum is \(|H|\).
Substitution into the weighted definition of
\(\mathcal R^\star_H\) yields the two rational expressions in the
statement; every coefficient in their final numerators is positive.

Finally, accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f` gives
\(U_1\subseteq R_1\) and \(U_2\subseteq R_2\).  Directly,
\(V\subseteq K\cap\{f_3\le0\}\), because both summands defining \(V\)
have nonpositive third shifted coordinate.  More basically, every
one of \(U_1,U_2,V\) is contained in
\((A_0+A_2)/2\).  Thus compatibility and convexity imply
\[
 H\subseteq K.
\]
The exact subtraction
\[
 |H|-(M+m)=\frac{5D^2-78D-179}{16}
\]
is positive at \(D=18\) and strictly increasing thereafter.  This
proves the no-half contradiction and completes the lemma.
statement:
Use the affine-plane and exact-cell convention of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`.  Let \(D\ge18\) be an integer, take \((s,t)\) as planar coordinates, and set
\[
 f_1(s,t)=\frac{s+t}{2},\qquad
 f_2(s,t)=\frac{t-s}{2},\qquad
 f_3(s,t)=-1-t,
\]
\[
 L_1=L_2=0,\qquad L_3=-D-1.
\]
Thus \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\) and
\(-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3)=D\).  Put \(C=D+2\), and define the rational triangles
\[
 A_0=\operatorname{conv}\left\{
 \left(-\frac{D+3}{2},\frac{D-1}{2}\right),
 \left(\frac{D+3}{2},\frac{D-1}{2}\right),
 (0,D+1)\right\},
\]
\[
 A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{(-2C,-C-2),(2C,-C-2),(0,-C+2)\}.
\]
Their exact cell areas are
\[
 p_1=p_2=p_3=1,\qquad
 p_\varnothing=\frac{(D+3)^2}{4}-3,
\]
with all other \(P\)-cells null, and
\[
 q_1=q_2=D,\qquad q_{123}=2D+4,\qquad q_{12}=4D+12,
\]
with all other \(Q\)-cells null.  In particular
\[
 M=|A_0|=\frac{(D+3)^2}{4},\qquad
 m=|A_2|=8(D+2),
\]
with \(M\ge m\) for every \(D\ge28\) and \(M/m\to\infty\), and the
positive \(Q\)-support is exactly
\(\{123,1,2,12\}\).

For \(i=1,2,3\), define
\[
 \Phi_i(a)=
 |A_0\cap\{f_i\le a\}|
 +|A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a\}|.
\]
Then
\[
 L_i=\inf\{a:\Phi_i(a)<\Phi_i(L_i)\}.
\]
Consequently, whenever constants \(c_i,h\) satisfy
\(h=c_i+\Phi_i(L_i)\), the level \(L_i\) is an actual lower crossing
in the sense of accepted fact `624b129b68e0fdee`.  All three endpoint
tails are strict:
\[
 \Phi_1(0)=\Phi_2(0)=7D+17<m,\qquad
 \Phi_3(-D-1)=2D+5<m.
\]

Take closures only to make the following polygons closed, which does
not change any area:
\[
 U_1=\frac{\overline{P_\varnothing}+\overline{Q_1}}2,\qquad
 U_2=\frac{\overline{P_\varnothing}+\overline{Q_2}}2,\qquad
 V=\frac{\overline{P_3}+\overline{Q_{123}}}2,
\]
\[
 H=\operatorname{conv}(U_1\cup U_2\cup V).
\]
The hull \(H\) is the symmetric rational nonagon whose vertices are
\[
 \left(-\frac{5D+9}{4},-\frac{D+7}{4}\right),\quad
 \left(-\frac{5D+7}{4},-\frac{D+9}{4}\right),\quad
 \left(-\frac{2D+5}{2},-2\right),
\]
\[
 \left(-\frac{D+2}{2},-\frac12\right),\quad
 \left(0,\frac12\right),
\]
together with the reflections in the line \(s=0\) of the first four
vertices.  Its area is
\[
 |H|=\frac{9D^2+74D+113}{16}.
\]

For \(G\ne\varnothing\), put
\[
\mathscr R_G=
\{f_i\le0\ (i\in G),\ f_i>0\ (i\notin G)\},
\qquad
h_G=|H\cap\mathscr R_G|.
\]
The complete list of nonzero values is
\[
 h_1=h_2=\frac{6D^2+29D+9}{24},
\qquad
 h_{12}=\frac{D^2+18D+65}{16},
\]
\[
 h_3=\frac{D+2}{4(D+4)},
\qquad
 h_{13}=h_{23}=
 \frac{13D^2+64D+54}{24(D+4)},
\qquad
 h_{123}=1.
\]
Therefore define the nonnegative weighted charge
\[
 \mathcal R^\star_H
 :=\frac32(h_1+h_2)+5h_{12}
 +\frac72(h_{13}+h_{23})+7h_{123}
 =
 \frac{51D^3+830D^2+4037D+6216}{48(D+4)},
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal R^\star_H-2p_\varnothing
 =
 \frac{27D^3+590D^2+3533D+6504}{48(D+4)}>0.
\]

If \(K\) is any convex body satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K,
\]
then \(H\subseteq K\).  For
\(r_G=|K\cap\mathscr R_G|\), define
\[
\mathcal R^\star_K
=\frac32(r_1+r_2)+5r_{12}
+\frac72(r_{13}+r_{23})+7r_{123}.
\]
Hence \(k=|K|\ge|H|\), while
\[
 |H|-(M+m)
 =\frac{5D^2-78D-179}{16}>0
 \qquad(D\ge18).
\]
Thus no such \(K\) can also satisfy the residual no-half inequality
\(k<M+m\).  Independently, since all \(R^\star\)-coefficients are
nonnegative, every compatible \(K\) satisfies
\(\mathcal R^\star_K\ge\mathcal R^\star_H>2p_\varnothing\).
